intro.title: Progressive Web Apps
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Progressive Web App (PWA) that works offline by caching resources. You'll learn how to use service workers to intercept network requests and serve cached content when there's no internet connection. The main technologies involved are JavaScript for the service worker logic and the Cache API for storing files. By the end, you'll have a web app that loads quickly and functions reliably, even in poor network conditions.
intro.usecase: Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) enable web applications to function like native mobile apps, providing offline access, push notifications, and home screen installation. You'll see this pattern in productivity tools like Google Docs and Figma, which work seamlessly even with poor internet connectivity. Social media platforms like Twitter Lite use PWAs to deliver fast, engaging experiences on low-end devices. As a frontend developer, implementing PWA features ensures your applications remain accessible and performant across diverse network conditions and devices.
